messages.speaker: human
messages.text: Today's focus: the atlas dashboard is too slow on large datasets. @researcher profile the slowest endpoint first.

messages.speaker: researcher
messages.text: Profiling done: /metrics/summary sits at 2.8s p95 on the 1M-row dataset. Query scans dominate.

messages.speaker: lead
messages.text: I propose we set a p95 target of 300ms for all dashboard endpoints on the 1M-row dataset.

messages.speaker: human
messages.text: Agreed, 300ms p95 is the target for dashboard endpoints.

messages.speaker: researcher
messages.text: Tentatively I want the in-process cache at 256MB, but let's confirm with a load test before locking it.

messages.speaker: lead
messages.text: Keep the cache in-process; no external cache server for the MVP.

messages.speaker: verifier
messages.text: Load test with a 256MB in-process cache: p95 dropped from 2.8s to 240ms. The size is workable.

messages.speaker: human
messages.text: Good: cache size is confirmed at 256MB, in-process only.

messages.speaker: lead
messages.text: Quick reminder: the dashboard p95 target we agreed is 300ms, keep it in the acceptance checklist.

messages.speaker: human
messages.text: What is our memory budget per pod? I don't want the cache to push us over.

messages.speaker: lead
messages.text: Budget is 512MB per pod; the 256MB cache fits with headroom.

messages.speaker: verifier
messages.text: Failure report: the nightly soak test crashed after 40 minutes; the pod restarted and the heap kept growing.

messages.speaker: researcher
messages.text: Found the leak: the cache never evicts expired keys, and entries hold references to full result sets.

messages.speaker: verifier
messages.text: Confirmed with heap dumps: missing eviction. After adding eviction, the soak test ran 6 hours stable.

messages.speaker: human
messages.text: Lesson for us: any cache we add must implement eviction from day one, never as a follow-up.

messages.speaker: lead
messages.text: Writing that into the design checklist.

messages.speaker: researcher
messages.text: What if we cached everything aggressively, every endpoint, near 100% hit ratio?

messages.speaker: lead
messages.text: That would burn memory and make invalidation a nightmare. No.

messages.speaker: human
messages.text: @lead please record this as a project rule: any new cache must ship with eviction and a hit-ratio metric.

messages.speaker: lead
messages.text: Rule recorded. I will add the hit-ratio metric to the service template.

messages.speaker: verifier
messages.text: Target check: we hold the 300ms p95 line after all changes.

messages.speaker: researcher
messages.text: Second finding: the aggregation query can go from 1.2s to 180ms with a pre-aggregated rollup table.

messages.speaker: human
messages.text: Do it: pre-aggregated rollup, refreshed every 5 minutes.

messages.speaker: lead
messages.text: Rollup pipeline is in; the refresh runs every 5 minutes as decided.

messages.speaker: verifier
messages.text: Verified: summary endpoint is now 210ms p95 on 1M rows.

messages.speaker: human
messages.text: For perf reports, send me before/after numbers in a table; that is how I read them.

messages.speaker: researcher
messages.text: I will draft the load-test report by Friday.

messages.speaker: lead
messages.text: I will extend the soak test to 12 hours overnight.

messages.speaker: verifier
messages.text: Running it; will report at standup.

messages.speaker: human
messages.text: Note for the report: use the same 1M-row dataset so the numbers stay comparable.

messages.speaker: researcher
messages.text: Understood, same dataset.

messages.speaker: human
messages.text: Good session. @verifier post the results tomorrow.

messages.speaker: verifier
messages.text: Will do.
